entry_state: Variable-fee changes distinguish pass-through value, unearned service and permitted mitigation. Partial reinsurance recovers only the allocated covered loss; later changes affect both groups without duplicate component entries. A changed contract requires its own derecognition and replacement-value analysis.
exit_state: A replacement premium transfers measurement without inventing cash. Future-service changes and finance use distinct rate bases. Variable-benefit allocation may require a revised rate, while changed holdings preserve the old OCI history under its own schedule.
findings: Equivalent premium 60 less actual extra premium 10 gives deemed premium 50. Old CSM becomes 20, new CSM 8, and cash increases only by 10.
The fixed-claim OCI path preserves total finance 21 and closes accumulated OCI at zero. The variable-benefit example instead needs allocation rate 20 percent to reach revised payment 144.
Held-item matching presents both sides separately; a change in holdings preserves prior OCI and its former assumptions rather than recomputing history. No new defect observed.
